name: hacklm-memory
description: Persistent memory layer for VS Code Copilot — learn from interactions, retain insights, improve over time

languageModelTools.name: hacklm-memory_storeMemory
languageModelTools.userDescription: Save a durable insight about this project for future sessions.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Store a durable insight about this project that would help in future sessions. Only store things that will matter next week. ALWAYS call queryMemory first to avoid duplicates. Always provide a slug (kebab-case topic key, e.g. 'console-logs'). Same slug = update, not duplicate. Categories: Instruction (how to behave), Quirk (project-specific weirdness), Preference (style/design choices), Decision (architectural commitments), Security (rules that must never be broken). After completing any implementation task, call this tool for each new decision, pattern, or convention applied — before ending the turn. Do not wait for the next queryMemory call.

content.description: The insight to store. Should be clear, actionable, and durable. Keep it to one concise line.

slug.description: A short kebab-case topic identifier (e.g. 'console-logs', 'async-style'). Same slug in the same category = overwrite, not duplicate.

languageModelTools.name: hacklm-memory_queryMemory
languageModelTools.userDescription: Search stored memories for relevant principles, preferences, and decisions.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Search stored memories for relevant principles, preferences, best practices, and decisions. Call this before answering questions about architecture, conventions, style, or any topic where prior context would help. Returns the most relevant entries ranked by keyword match and recency. After returning results, if your previous response produced project-specific learnings not yet stored, call storeMemory before proceeding.

query.description: Search query — keywords or a natural language question

category.description: Optional: filter to a specific category

viewsWelcome.contents:
No memories stored yet.

Copilot will save insights here as you chat. You can also open the control panel to manage memories manually.

[Open Control Panel](command:hacklm-memory.panel)

walkthroughs.title: Get started with HackLM Memory
walkthroughs.description: Set up persistent memory for Copilot — takes about 2 minutes.

steps.title: How it works
steps.description: HackLM Memory gives Copilot a persistent memory layer across sessions. Your project's conventions, decisions, and preferences are stored in `.memory/` and injected on every new chat.

steps.title: Open the Memories view
steps.description:
Find stored memories in the Explorer sidebar.
[Open Memories View](command:hacklm-memory.memoriesView.focus)

steps.title: Store your first memory
steps.description:
Open Copilot Chat and tell it something worth remembering. It will call `storeMemory` automatically.
[Open Copilot Chat](command:workbench.action.chat.open)

steps.title: Configure your language model
steps.description:
Choose which Copilot model powers deduplication and gap analysis. Skip if `gpt-5-mini` works for you.
[Open Control Panel](command:hacklm-memory.panel)

steps.title: You're set up
steps.description:
HackLM Memory is active. Open the control panel any time to browse, clean, or review your memories.
[Open Control Panel](command:hacklm-memory.panel)

hacklm-memory.autoCleanupFrequency.markdownDescription: Run automatic cleanup after this many `storeMemory` calls.

hacklm-memory.categoryLimit.Instruction.markdownDescription: Max entries to keep in the `Instruction` category.

hacklm-memory.categoryLimit.Quirk.markdownDescription: Max entries to keep in the `Quirk` category.

hacklm-memory.categoryLimit.Preference.markdownDescription: Max entries to keep in the `Preference` category.

hacklm-memory.categoryLimit.Decision.markdownDescription: Max entries to keep in the `Decision` category.
